core_obligations: Prove case (1) through the generic point description (proof lines 6524-6530).
Prove case (2) by taking a nonzero element at every generic point and multiplying (proof lines 6530-6538).
Record case (3) as the cited Noetherian statement (proof lines 6538-6541).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: an invertible module L on X has a regular meromorphic section when X is integral, or X is reduced with finitely many irreducible components in every quasi-compact open, or X is locally Noetherian without embedded points (source lines 6510-6522). In case (1) the generic point argument identifies K_X and K_X(L) with the constant (skyscraper) sheaves at the generic point, so a nonzero element of the one-dimensional fibre is a regular meromorphic section; in case (2) the same is done at every generic point and the product is shown to be a regular meromorphic section using the description of the two sheaves; case (3) is the Noetherian statement which the author cites by name.
